title: Host-wide concurrent run cap (issue #1932)
goal: Add a configurable, fail-open, off-by-default host-wide counted cap on concurrent pipeline runs, with explicit refusal naming blockers, dead-holder reaping, and an operator override — amending ADR-059 §4 with a new §7 section.

steps.description: Create core/state/run-cap.sh — the cap module. Implements: zbuild_run_cap_slot_dir (returns ${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT}/run-slots); zbuild_run_cap_reap_stale (scan slot dir, call zbuild_run_is_live on each PID-keyed entry, delete stale ones, fail-open); zbuild_run_cap_count_live [exclude_pid] (count live slot files excluding given PID, fail-open returns count via stdout); zbuild_run_cap_write_slot <run_id> [state_file] (write <slot_dir>/$$.json with run_id, pid, state_file, acquired_at); zbuild_run_cap_release (remove <slot_dir>/$$.json); zbuild_run_cap_admit <run_id> [state_file] (the admission gate: no-op if ZBUILD_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS unset; admits with warning if ZBUILD_NO_RUN_CAP=1; mkdir slot_dir fail-open; reap stale fail-open; count live excluding $$ fail-open — on error warn+return 0; if count >= cap set _ZBUILD_RUN_CAP_BLOCKERS and return 1; else write slot return 0). Sources resume.sh for zbuild_run_is_live.

Modify core/pipeline/runner.sh to integrate the cap. Three changes: (1) source run-cap.sh alongside issue-lock.sh near the top of the file; (2) in main(), call zbuild_run_cap_admit before the issue lock acquire (lines ~2297-2310), emit pipeline.refused.run_cap event and a named-blocker error message on refusal, return 1; (3) in _runner_abort_trap() (the exit trap, ~line 2470), call zbuild_run_cap_release alongside zbuild_issue_lock_release.

Create tests/unit/run-cap-test.sh covering all issue-required specs: [SPEC-1] ZBUILD_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS unset — admit returns 0 and writes no slot file (byte-identically unaffected guard); [SPEC-2] cap+1 starts — pre-populate cap live slots, attempt one more, expect refusal naming blockers (reddens at merge-base); [SPEC-3] fail-open — inject a counting error (unreadable slot dir) and confirm the run is admitted with a warning; [SPEC-4] ZBUILD_NO_RUN_CAP=1 override — admits regardless of cap; [SPEC-5] dead holder reaping — write a slot with a dead PID/stale state, confirm it is reaped before counting and does not block admission.

Amend docs/adr/ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md. Add a new ### 7 section under Decision (dated 2026-10-10): 'Host-wide run cap, off unless configured' — states the rule (flat run count, off unless ZBUILD_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS set, fail-open, dead holders reaped with zbuild_run_is_live before counting, override via ZBUILD_NO_RUN_CAP, refusal names blockers, race window on no-flock hosts stated not hidden). Add an entry for §7 to the existing ## Enforced by section naming tests/unit/run-cap-test.sh and its five spec statements.

notes: 1. Placement of cap check vs issue lock: cap check (zbuild_run_cap_admit) is placed BEFORE the issue lock acquire in runner.sh — cap is a coarser resource gate and should fail fast. 2. Race window: two runs racing with no-flock cannot both be serialised by the PID-file approach alone; with count-then-write they may both proceed past a cap of 1. This mirrors the no-flock weakness already stated in issue-lock.sh and should be documented in §7 the same way. 3. 'A run never counts itself' — the admission count excludes the calling run's own $$ because the slot is written only after admission passes; on the happy path no slot exists yet for this PID. 4. Fail-open scope: mkdir failure, unreadable entries, missing zbuild_run_is_live function, unexpected ps output — all warn to stderr and return 0 from zbuild_run_cap_admit. Only a successful count above the cap refuses. 5. Release in exit trap: zbuild_run_cap_release must run even if slot was never written (no-op in that case, guarded by -f check). 6. The issue says 'State the red step in the PR body' — the plan step produces a test that reddens at merge-base because no run-cap.sh exists yet; the PR description should record this. 7. ADR-059 amendment adds §7 as a dated subsection inside the existing Decision section; the ## Enforced by section already exists and gains one new bullet. 8. ZBUILD_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS is the env var name stated in the issue Constraints; ZBUILD_NO_RUN_CAP=1 follows the ZBUILD_NO_ISSUE_LOCK=1 pattern from issue-lock.sh.
